item.title: Oregon family renovates free abandoned mobile home for $14k so mom and twins host Thanksgiving
item.description: An Oregon family took on the challenge of revamping a deserted mobile home into a cozy space for their relatives. Lyman Branson II and his family poured months of effort into fixing the property for Betty Branson and her daughters. Despite budget hurdles, they created a safe haven. Just in time for Thanksgiving, they received the occupancy certificate, allowing them to celebrate their first holiday together in their new home.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ohio court says lawyers must prove fair fees after client secures $250,000 car settlement herself
item.description: Amber Kopanski settled her car crash claim directly with Progressive Direct Insurance Company for $250,000 after parting ways with her lawyers. Her former law firm, Rumizen Weisman Co., Ltd., sought payment for its legal fees and costs after her settlement. The appeals court ruled that the firm cannot simply apply its contract percentage for payment determination.

item.title: Florida court overturns fraud findings in $34.7m tobacco death case, orders new damages trial
item.description: In a significant development, Frances Bessent-Dixon's lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds was impacted by a recent court ruling. The appeals court dismissed the prior jury's fraud verdict, necessitating a new trial focused on damages. Tyrone M. Dixon, Bessent-Dixon's late husband, passed away from throat cancer caused by smoking, with R.J. Reynolds asserting that he was aware of the dangers of tobacco.

item.title: 28 ancient Gallic coins and skull fragments hint at lost sanctuary in France
item.description: Archaeologists exploring Bure in northeastern France uncovered 28 ancient Gallic coins alongside human skull fragments. The site is believed to be a Late Iron Age sanctuary used by the Leuci. In addition to the coins, a miniature bronze wagon wheel was also found, suggesting ritual significance. The discovery contributes to understanding the cultural and religious practices of ancient Gaul. Ongoing studies aim to clarify the site's history and purpose.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Jolly Cheery’s Journey: Tree travels with low-emission transport; tradition links Norway and Britain
item.description: This year, London welcomes a spectacular 21-metre Norwegian spruce named Jolly Cheery for its Christmas display. Selected through public voting, this tree represents the enduring friendship between Norway and the UK. To minimize environmental impact, it will be transported in an eco-friendly manner and adorned with energy-efficient lights, set to be unveiled on December 3. Post-Christmas, it will be composted, promoting sustainability.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: English detectorist finds rare 380-year-old coin in Essex field after months of searching
item.description: Discoveries like this don't happen every day! A metal detector enthusiast in Essex came across a remarkable silver coin, dating to 1646, in a farmer's field. Dubbed a siege piece from the English Civil War that spanned 1642 to 1651, the coin bears the initials of King Charles I, suggesting a Royalist connection.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Funeral director wins A$48,966 after employer sacks him over police clearance
item.description: A 65-year-old Australian funeral director was dismissed after police revoked a clearance required for body-transfer duties he had stopped performing months earlier. The Fair Work Commission found the dismissal unfair, noting that the employee was unlikely to resume the work and that the employer had not properly challenged the police decision.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 314 years after Dutch ship sank off Australia, 23 stolen silver coins return from California and Amsterdam
item.description: After extensive efforts, Australia has reclaimed twenty-three silver coins from the infamous Zuytdorp shipwreck, which was lost at sea in 1712. The recovery operations spanned both the Netherlands and the United States, revealing a surge in illicit interest since 2019. In light of this, Australian authorities ramped up their monitoring, culminating in local resident Ashley Patterson's guilty plea for breaching underwater heritage laws linked to these invaluable artifacts.

item.title: Federal Appeals Court reopens Trump's route to challenge his New York conviction
item.description: In a surprising turn of events, Donald Trump’s legal team has been afforded a fresh opportunity to challenge his criminal conviction. A federal appeals court has chosen to revisit his application to shift jurisdiction from New York. This could pave the way for Trump to assert presidential immunity, potentially leading to an overturn of his conviction.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tamworth Castle restorers uncover 1960s cigarette packet and hidden treasures
item.description: The £1.9 million restoration of Tamworth Castle is revealing intriguing historical artifacts. Among the recent discoveries are a cigarette packet from the 1950s and a 1968 newspaper, shedding light on the lives of its past inhabitants. Additionally, restorers found an 18th or 19th-century lead-lined sink, enhancing our understanding of the castle's historical usage.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Coastal Topi Numbers Rebound: Raabia Hawa wins Tusk award; ranger teams and communities protect ecosystems
item.description: Raabia Hawa has been honored with the 2026 Tusk Award for her exceptional dedication to wildlife conservation. As a former radio personality, she pivoted her career to enhance efforts in protecting endangered species in Kenya. Through her founded Ulinzi Africa Foundation, she has championed anti-poaching campaigns, directly aiding in the resurgence of coastal topi populations, and emphasizing the essential role of community engagement in conservation success.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California recycling business faces eviction after Metro buys leased land for light rail project, appeals court rules
item.description: A recycling company in Van Nuys is contesting its eviction following the acquisition of its property by the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority. The California Court of Appeal has decided that the sale to Metro terminated the existing lease. The business owners argued that eminent domain processes should have applied, but the court disagreed, allowing Metro's unlawful detainer case to continue.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ashley Cain's Foundation raises £3 million for childhood cancer research and treatment
item.description: In loving memory of their daughter, Azaylia Diamond Cain, Ashley Cain and Safiyya Vorajee founded The Azaylia Foundation. This charity is dedicated to enhancing childhood cancer treatment and funding research, having raised over £3 million since its launch. With its commitment to boosting early diagnosis and innovative therapies, the foundation collaborates with UK universities and offers Treatment Pathway Grants to broaden treatment options.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 17-year-old's website lets people send messages from beyond the grave
item.description: 17-year-old Alice Footer from Australia's Gold Coast has developed FromBeyond.co, a website that lets people record personal messages and schedule their delivery to loved ones on birthdays, Christmas and other occasions, even after their death. Inspired by her grandmother's stories and worried that younger family members might lose touch with their family's past, Alice created the platform to preserve memories for future generations.

item.title: Florida couple's $2.77 million custom home project never began; appeals court reverses $126,624 damages award
item.description: A couple in Florida faced a reversal of a damages award related to their failed construction project. They had originally paid $257,500 towards a custom home that was never built. The appeals court decided that their claims should be resolved through arbitration, as stipulated in their construction agreement. Allegations of fraudulent misrepresentation against the construction company's owners were thus addressed in this ruling.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: How two Chinese nationals and their sons cheated US Medicare and Medicaid of $55 million
item.description: Two Chinese nationals and their sons have been indicted in the US over an alleged $55 million Medicare and Medicaid fraud scheme. Prosecutors claim the Queens-based family billed government health programmes for unnecessary medicines, including pain patches, and paid beneficiaries cash and supermarket gift cards to fill prescriptions. The family allegedly used shell companies and fake pharmacy ownership records to conceal the money, which was spent on properties, investments, cryptocurrency and luxury vehicles.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: AI Identifies Three Brain Patterns: Stanford study finds 3 child biotypes; patterns may inform targeted care
item.description: Stanford Medicine researchers identified three distinct brain patterns in children diagnosed with ADHD and anxiety. Their study suggests differences in brain connectivity can predict the development of these conditions. Researchers analyzed data from children aged 9 to 11 in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study. The findings may lead to more tailored treatment approaches for those experiencing attention and emotional difficulties.
